_note: Scenario prompts: the agent answers as the assistant would act, without running anything. Taken from the first combined-session packet, which followed a manager-plus-implementer pilot.

evals.prompt: The owner approved one bounded change on the ledger project and said: run it as a combined fast lane, one sol session for both roles, and tell me what it cost. The worktree is /home/dev/p/ledger-slice on branch slice/ledger-1, clean. Your packet folder is /var/tmp/ledger-manager/packet-s1/. What do you write and run, in order, to get the session started, and how will you know the cost at the end?
evals.expected_output: Writes config.json (name, worktree, optional scans and identity), writes a one-page self-contained task.md from the template, starts with scripts/session.sh PKT and waits with fastlane's wait.sh. Sets no cap, checkpoint or stop. At close-out takes three meter readings: session, review and the assistant's own transcript, in new tokens.
expectations: Writes a self-contained task.md that tells the session not to commit or push, and to launch models only through the reviewer launcher
Starts the session with scripts/session.sh PKT rather than a hand-written codex command
Sets no token cap, checkpoint or stop, and does not tell the session to ration its reading
Plans three meter readings at close-out: the session, the reviewers, and the assistant's own session
Reports new tokens (uncached input plus output), with totals as a diagnostic only
Creates waits at the packet root so session and review units enter the shared wait record
Keeps the test suspension in the task and session until the live test passes
The session fills the fixed brief, launches reviewers, waits, judges and repairs in its turn; the assistant reads the report and final round
Session and reviewer meters use the combined session id to avoid double-counting; names missing Grok measurement if unavailable

evals.prompt: Combined fast lane, packet folder /var/tmp/shop-manager/packet-c2/. The session's first turn ended with 'HANDOFF: partial': the new module fails to build with one type error at cart.rs:88, and the handoff says the fix needs a decision between two ways to model a discount. The owner picked the second way. What do you do next?
evals.expected_output: Writes a short note file with the owner's answer and the next step, and runs scripts/session.sh PKT NOTE_FILE to resume the same session; does not start a fresh session or a separate implementer, and does not hand-run codex; then waits on the new turn's folder.
expectations: Resumes the same session with scripts/session.sh PKT NOTE_FILE instead of starting a new session
Says why: the session's history comes back from cache, so nothing is read in twice
The note states the owner's decision and the next step, and that the task and its rules still stand
Does not fix the build error itself in the worktree while the session owns it
Waits on the new turn's folder with fastlane's wait.sh

evals.prompt: You are the combined sol session. You built the uncommitted candidate, filled the fixed brief and ran the reviewers. The required reviewers answered; opus reports one P1 (the refusal check compares a value with itself, so it cannot fail) and two P3s. You read the code: the refusal type carries no state, so the check is redundant rather than wrong, and you think it is a P3. What happens next, and who decides?
evals.expected_output: The session judges each finding and writes judgement.md, but must end its turn with the proposed lowering and file:line evidence for the owner. The assistant relays that call and does not judge. P3s stay as follow-ups. The same session resumes with the owner's decision; if it remains P1 the session repairs and re-reviews the delta before the assistant runs close.py.
expectations: Ends the session turn with the proposed lowering of the reviewer's P1 and file:line evidence for the owner
The session judges findings; the assistant relays the owner call without judging
Writes judgement.md with one line per finding: the reviewer's rating, the judge's rating, the evidence and where it went
Files the P3 findings as follow-ups and does not fix them in this change, even if the session is resumed
If a repair is needed, resumes through scripts/session.sh with a note naming only the verified P0/P1
Judges before close.py commits, then deploys and runs the live test only after review clears

evals.prompt: You are the combined sol session and the packet built successfully. What panel do you launch and wait on in your turn? Grok is installed but its one-word probe fails. Sol fails twice. Fable is still running. Can you proceed, and what happens next?
evals.expected_output: Uses the shared fastlane panel: opus, astra, sol plus grok only after an answering probe; fable optional. Waits on launched required seats, relaunches a failed seat once, proceeds if opus and astra answered, names sol and grok missing, never waits for fable. Judges findings before a scanned close.py commit, then deploys and live-tests.
expectations: Defaults to opus astra sol and grok when available, never one reviewer
Requires an answering one-word grok -p probe before launching grok; reports failed probe missing without waiting or blocking
Relaunches sol once; with two of opus/astra/sol answered can continue and names sol missing
Never waits for fable
The session launches the reviewer script, which runs the grok probe; the assistant does not launch reviewers or judge
Review and judgment precede close.py commit, which precedes the live test

evals.prompt: A bounded combined packet needs a second live iteration. A reviewer also flagged missing unit-test coverage and two P2s. The next live run passes. Describe repair, review, evidence and test handling without starting another session.
evals.expected_output: Resumes the same session with the live failures, defers test-only findings and P2s, re-reviews the delta with earlier findings and followups, checks the reviewed diff hash before close.py commit, deploys and live-tests, cleans up, reads the post-live receipt for close-out, then restores suspended tests using FASTLANE_TESTS=on on a resume.
expectations: Resumes the same combined session; bounded live iterations are supported
Defers missing coverage to deferred-tests.md and P2s to followups.md without repairing them
Uses fastlane review format, exact P0-P3 lines, delta and earlier findings for re-review
Checks diff hash before close.py commits, then runs live test and cleanup
Brings tests back after live pass with updated task and FASTLANE_TESTS=on on the resumed session
Receipt is post-live evidence for close-out, never a prerequisite for review
Reads the exact template from the source path named in the session prompt and filled task
Retries and re-reviews pass fresh --out and --tag; waits and Grok availability paths use that current output, never an earlier round's exits

evals.prompt: You are the combined sol session, 35 minutes into a six-hour turn. Two of the task's three parts build and pass; the third, a proof, is not written yet. You have listed the six lemmas it needs and tried none. The task says to stop partial if the proof cannot be finished. A reviewer-style read of your own code also shows two required message steps are missing. What do you do?
evals.expected_output: Keeps working: remaining work is not a named obstacle, so it attempts the lemmas and adds the missing required steps in this turn. It launches no reviewers on the unfinished candidate and makes no owner call for a fix the task already requires. It stops partial only with a counterexample, a specific step with what was tried and why it failed, something reserved for the assistant or owner, or the time limit, and reviews only once all three parts are complete.
expectations: Does not stop: an untried proof with a known plan is remaining work, not a named obstacle
Launches no reviewers until the candidate is complete
Fixes the missing required steps in the turn instead of raising them as an owner call
Names what would justify a partial stop: a counterexample, one specific failed step with attempts, a reserved run or decision, or the time limit
If it does stop partial, the handoff names the obstacle and one precise remaining goal
Collects and judges every launched required reader before ending a turn
